title: Cut clips on the Timeline
summary: Split clips with the Razor tool, remove a piece without a gap, and cut at the playhead.

steps.say: Click an empty spot in the Timeline at the bottom right so it has focus.

check.prompt: Is the Timeline panel at the bottom right outlined in blue as the active panel, with clips on it?

hints: The Timeline is the panel with the V1 and A1 track rows. A blue outline shows it is active.
If the Timeline is empty, drag a clip from the Project panel into it first.
steps.why: Premiere sends shortcuts to the panel with focus, so the Timeline must be active.

steps.say: Press C to pick the Razor tool.

checks.prompt: Is the razor blade tool highlighted in the Tools panel, or is the pointer a razor blade?

hints: The Razor tool looks like a razor blade in the thin Tools strip next to the Timeline.
Click the Timeline first if the key does nothing.
steps.why: The Razor tool cuts a clip wherever you click.

steps.say: Click on a clip in the Timeline where you want to split it.

check.prompt: Is there a new cut line splitting a clip in the Timeline?

hints: Hover over the clip; a line shows where the cut will go. Click once.
Hold Shift while clicking to cut every track at that point.
steps.why: Splitting a clip lets you remove or move part of it.

steps.say: Press V to switch back to the Selection tool.

checks.prompt: Is the arrow Selection tool highlighted in the Tools panel?

hints: V is the arrow at the top of the Tools strip.
With the Razor still active every click makes another cut, so switch now.
steps.why: The Selection tool lets you pick clips without cutting them.

steps.say: Click the piece of the clip you want to remove.

check.prompt: Is one piece of the cut clip highlighted as selected in the Timeline?

hints: A selected clip turns a lighter shade. Click once without dragging.
Click an empty area to clear the selection and try again.
steps.why: Premiere deletes only what is selected.

steps.say: Press Shift Delete to remove it and close the gap. Control Z undoes it.

checks.prompt: Has the selected piece gone, with the later clips moved left so no gap remains?

hints: Plain Delete leaves an empty gap. Holding Shift closes it.
You can also right click the clip and choose Ripple Delete.
steps.why: Ripple delete keeps the edit tight with no black gaps.

steps.say: Move the playhead to a new spot, then press Control K to cut without changing tools.

checks.prompt: Is there a new cut on the clip exactly under the playhead?

hints: Click in the time ruler above the tracks to move the playhead.
Control K cuts the targeted tracks; Control Shift K cuts all tracks.
steps.why: Cutting at the playhead is faster than switching to the Razor tool each time.
